title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of lung cancer and new bone pain.

HPI
The patient is an 81-year-old female who presents today for a follow-up evaluation regarding her cancer of the right lung. She is currently receiving chemotherapy and reports that she has been feeling a dull, aching sensation in her lower spine over the past three weeks. She describes the pain as constant but manageable with over-the-counter measures, though it has become more pronounced during movement. She denies any new shortness of breath, productive cough, or significant weight loss since her last appointment. She reports that her energy levels remain stable despite the ongoing treatment.

Medication List
- Prednisone 10mg daily
- Ondansetron 8mg as needed for nausea
- Acetaminophen 650mg as needed for pain

Review of Systems
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or night sweats.
Respiratory: No shortness of breath or cough.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for localized back pain.
Neurological: No numbness or tingling in extremities.

Social History
The patient lives at home with her daughter. She is a retired teacher and enjoys gardening and light walking. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Type 2 Diabetes.
Father: Hypertension.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.4 F
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 78 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 96% on room air
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 11.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.4 x 10^9/L
Platelets: 180 x 10^9/L
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented.
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Tenderness noted upon palpation of the lumbar spine. No focal neurological deficits.

Assessment
1. Cancer of the right lung: Patient is currently receiving chemotherapy.
2. Bone metastases: New onset of spinal pain suggests progression of the malignant neoplasm to the skeletal system.

Plan
1. Continue current chemotherapy regimen as scheduled.
2. Order a skeletal survey and a dedicated MRI of the lumbar spine to confirm the extent of the bone metastasis.
3. Start scheduled physical therapy for pain management.
4. Follow up in two weeks to review imaging and adjust pain management.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, DO, 10/14/2026
explanations: Cancer of the right lung under current treatment is a current malignancy: C34.91.
Bone metastases: C79.51, secondary malignant neoplasm of bone (HCC 18, which outranks the primary-site HCC).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
The note documents the right lung: use the right-lung code.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in bone, not the liver.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Bone/Other and Unspecified Metastatic Cancer; Acute Leukemia Except Myeloid
